claims.text: A nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy can display high thermal stability.
A nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy can resist heavy-ion irradiation, dual-beam irradiation, and helium implantation with low defect evolution and no detectable grain growth.
The proposed baseline nanocrystalline RHEA has limited yield strength and ductility under extreme conditions.
A heat-treatment and alloying strategy can induce stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations in a tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy.
The induced nanoprecipitates have coherent interfaces with the tungsten RHEA matrix.
The nanoprecipitate interfacial phases are thin.
The nanoprecipitate interfacial phases remain stable under high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could initiate premature cracks.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation improves the strength-ductility combination of tungsten RHEAs.
Coherent interfaces minimize interface decohesion.
The coherent nanoprecipitates preserve grain integrity under irradiation.
The coherent nanoprecipitates increase resistance to irradiation-induced defects.
Relative to a precipitate-free baseline, the modified alloy will have higher yield strength at approximately 800 °C or above.
Relative to a precipitate-free baseline, the modified alloy will have greater tensile ductility at approximately 800 °C or above.
The mechanical benefits will persist under heavy-ion or neutron irradiation.
Adding coherent nanoprecipitates will preserve thermal stability at a level similar to the precipitate-free baseline.
Adding coherent nanoprecipitates will preserve irradiation resistance at a level similar to the precipitate-free baseline.
The benefit requires careful control of precipitate size, volume fraction, and spatial distribution.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or loss of coherence could degrade mechanical performance and irradiation resistance.

contradictions.description: The intervention includes an alloying strategy, which ordinarily changes composition, while the experiment specifies that both groups use the same composition. It is unclear whether alloying is common to both groups or is part of the differential intervention.
